name: Yellow-rattle
grown_as: A wild annual of hay meadows, sown in the grass to weaken it: it is half a parasite, taking water and food from grass roots.
habit: A stiff upright annual 10 to 50 cm, the stem single or with a few side branches, often streaked or spotted black, standing up among the grass.

leaf.outline: Narrowly oblong to lance-shaped, 1 to 5 cm long
leaf.margin: Regular, coarse, forward-pointing teeth all along both sides
leaf.colour: Dark green, often tinged bronze or purple

flower.form: A small two-lipped tube: a hooded upper lip, flattened side to side, over a smaller three-lobed lower lip
flower.petals: Joined into one tube, opening into the two lips; two tiny violet teeth at the tip of the hood
flower.colour: Yellow, with the two small violet teeth
flower.behind: A large, flattened, inflated green calyx, almost round, from which the yellow tube pokes
flower.carried: In a leafy spike at the stem tops, all turned to one side, each flower above a triangular bract with long sharp teeth

fruit: The calyx dries to a round, flat, papery straw-brown purse around a round flat capsule; the ripe seeds rattle inside when shaken. Seeds flat, round, 3 to 5 mm, brown, with a papery wing all round.
seedling: Comes up in late winter or early spring after the seed has had weeks of cold. Two narrow oval seed leaves, then opposite pairs of small toothed leaves.
winter: None: an annual, gone by late summer.

leaf: narrow stalkless leaf with coarse regular teeth all along
bloom: a yellow two-lipped flower with a hood
two tiny violet teeth on the hood
a large flat inflated green calyx behind
seed: flat round brown seeds with a papery wing all round
seedling: first true leaves an opposite pair, toothed
young: an upright stem with opposite pairs of narrow toothed leaves
flower: upright stems with a leafy spike of yellow hooded flowers on one side
seedhead: stiff brown stems carrying flat round papery straw-coloured purses

look_alikes: Greater yellow-rattle (Rhinanthus angustifolius) is rarer and larger, with a longer, curved flower tube. Common cow-wheat (Melampyrum pratense) has narrow untoothed leaves, flowers in pairs and no inflated calyx. Red bartsia has pink flowers.
